messages:
anya-support: Hey team, BrightLabs reported their console shows zero activity for the last 6 hours while their API logs show requests went through. Screenshot attached in the ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/BL-301. Can we triage?

michael-eng: Thanks Anya. Can you paste the tenant id and a quick repro? Also need ETL/consumer lag indicators.

anya-support: Tenant: brightlabs-prod (tenant_id=tb_89f3). Repro: open Console -> Usage -> select last 24h -> counts drop to 0 after 2026-03-17 03:00 UTC. API success logs: "200 OK" for events at 03:10, 03:20.

sre-bot: alert: etl-consumer-lag (ingest-consumer-1) breached 00:40:00 window at 2026-03-17T03:15:12Z. Offset lag: 12,000 msgs.

michael-eng: Ok looks like a consumer lag around that time. @sarah-data can you check the backfill job that ran overnight? Job id? any timeouts?

sarah-data: Backfill job id: bf_20260317_02. It started at 02:50 UTC. Partial completion: processed partitions 0-5, timed out on 6-9 due to GC spikes. Error excerpt: ```java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space at com.redwood.etl.BatchConsumer.process(BatchConsumer.java:412)``` We retried once and the retry aborted after 15m (deadline).

josh-support: Customer is on a tight SL window — they just pinged again. They saw undocumented spikes in "daily active tokens" metric specifically.

michael-eng: Sarah, can you paste the consumer group offsets around 03:00? run: ```kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-prod:9092 --group ingest-v2 --describe --offsets --members```

sarah-data: Ran it, summary: partition 6-9 laged ~12000 msgs at 03:05. Partition 6 had last consumed offset 145230 vs log end 157245. Full csv snippet: ```partition,committed,log_end,lag
6,145230,157245,12015
7,145000,156900,11900```

michael-eng: That matches the window where Console rollups missed hourly writes. Quick check: run this SQL to count rows in hourly_rollups for that tenant: ```SELECT hour, count(*) FROM hourly_rollups WHERE tenant_id='tb_89f3' AND hour >= '2026-03-17' GROUP BY hour ORDER BY hour;```

sarah-data: Query result: hours 00:00-03:00 have rows, 04:00-09:00 are empty. It aligns with the consumer lag and partial backfill stop.

anya-support: Repro steps for customer: they call ListUsage API -> backend returns counts -> Console query for rollups yields zeros. Customer impact: brightlabs-prod dashboards show zeros from 03:00-09:00.

michael-eng: Root cause summary: overnight backfill timed out while consumer lag grew due to GC/heap OOM; partial backfill left partitions unprocessed so hourly rollups never wrote for those hours. Plan: 1) run targeted backfill for tenant and missing hours, 2) pin to a worker with increased heap and monitoring, 3) add retry with exponential backoff for that job.

sarah-data: I can trigger targeted rehydrate for tenant tb_89f3 for hours 2026-03-17T04:00..2026-03-17T09:00 with job bf_replay_small --tenant tb_89f3 --hours 4-9 --force --worker-type=highmem. Proposed command: ```./bin/backfill --job bf_replay_small --tenant tb_89f3 --start 2026-03-17T04:00 --end 2026-03-17T09:00 --workers 2 --worker-profile highmem```

michael-eng: Do it, but add --dry-run first and confirm expected row counts. Also create a safety lock to prevent double-apply (idempotency token).

sarah-data: Dry-run shows ~28k events to replay. Proceeding with real run now. Job queued: bf_replay_small_4729.

deploy-bot: job bf_replay_small_4729 started on worker highmem-07 at 2026-03-17T04:40:12Z. Logs: https://etl.redwood.ai/jobs/bf_replay_small_4729/logs

sarah-data: Job completed successfully at 2026-03-17T05:02:18Z. Post-run check: hourly_rollups now have rows for 04:00-09:00. SQL verification: ```SELECT hour, count(*) FROM hourly_rollups WHERE tenant_id='tb_89f3' AND hour BETWEEN '2026-03-17T04:00' AND '2026-03-17T09:00' ORDER BY hour;``` returns non-zero counts.

anya-support: Great — I'll update BrightLabs that we've restored their metrics and explain cause + mitigation. Can we add a customer-facing note and a postmortem?

michael-eng: Yes. Action items: (a) Sarah to harden backfill memory profiling and increase default heap for heavy jobs, (b) Infra to add auto-scaler for GC pressure (c) Add health-check to alert earlier when consumer lag > 10k for > 10m, route to oncall. I'll draft a short postmortem and ping for review.

josh-support: Thanks all — customer notified. They appreciated the quick fix :thumbsup:

anya-support: Closing the escalation once PM/ops ack on postmortem. Leaving thread open for the next 24h for regressions.
